title: Exhibit
description: Application-neutral representation of a philatelic exhibit's structure.

spec_version.description: Semver of this format, not of the exhibit or any application.

id.description: Optional stable identifier for this exhibit instance (e.g. a UUID).

author.description: Both fields optional; present the object only if at least one is known.

class.description: Primary exhibit class. Shared vocabulary across federations: the FIP-style classes plus the classes that exist in APS (or another federation) but not in FIP. Whether a given ruleset accepts a given class is that ruleset's business, not this schema's.

youth_age_group.description: Age group of a youth exhibitor: a, b or c (the youth rules' three bands). Required when class is "youth", not allowed for any other class. Which traditional/thematic treatment the youth exhibit follows goes in the ruleset's `subclass`.

rulesets.description: Judging rulesets this exhibit targets. An exhibit may target more than one federation (e.g. FIP and APS) at once; each carries its own subclass taxonomy.

synopsis.description: The exhibit's synopsis/plan as text. Use this OR `synopsis_pages`, not both.

synopsis_pages.description: The synopsis as page images, for a synopsis that only exists as a scanned or designed document. Use this OR `synopsis`, not both. Pages are in reading order.

page_number.description: 1-indexed page number. Optional: when omitted, the array order is the page order.

allOf.description: youth_age_group is required for the youth class and forbidden for every other class.

ruleset_ref.description: Reference to a judging ruleset. The ruleset's own criteria/rubric are not part of this format.

name.description: e.g. FIP, APS, FEPA, FIAP. Open vocabulary, not enumerated.

subclass.description: Subclass label within `class`, per this ruleset's own taxonomy (e.g. FIP Postal History "2C", APS Revenue "fiscal_history", youth "traditional"). Meaning and validity are ruleset-specific and not enforced by this schema.

size.description: Preset is a shorthand; dimensions_mm is the escape hatch for non-standard sizes. At least one is required. When both are present, dimensions_mm wins.

uri.description: Absolute URI of the image. A consumer fetches it, so it must be reachable by the consumer for as long as the consumer needs it: producers that keep images private should hand out time-limited (signed) URIs.

media_type.description: Optional hint; the consumer should still check the fetched content.

checksum.description: Recommended: lets a consumer verify what it fetched is what the producer described.

frame_number.description: 1-indexed position of this frame within the exhibit.

grid_cols.description: Columns of the widest row when `rows` is present.

rows.description: Optional per-row layout, for frames whose rows differ (e.g. a row of four A4 sheets above a row of three Square sheets). rows[i] describes grid row i. When present: rows.length equals grid_rows, grid_cols equals the largest `cols`, and a sheet's position.col + colspan must not exceed its row's `cols`. When absent every row has grid_cols columns of the same base cell size, taken from the sheets' `size`.

size.description: Size of this row's base cell.
